subject: humpback whale
title: Humpback Whales Team Up in 4s to Trap Fish Hiding in the Sand

scenes.text: These fish hide from whales in sand. Not anymore.
Scientists stuck cameras on humpback whales off Massachusetts.
They filmed a hundred and ten seafloor hunts. In four out of five, the whale had partners.
Two to four whales sink down and close in until their snouts almost touch.
The fish get squeezed into the middle, and the whales open their mouths almost together.
It's the first time humpbacks were seen teaming up down there. The sand isn't safe anymore.

description:
Small sand lance fish escape predators by burying themselves in the seafloor, but humpback whales in the Gulf of Maine have learned to hunt them there as a team.
Video tags on seven whales recorded 110 seafloor hunts; in 87 of them (about 79%) the whale hunted with one to three partners, closing in head to head with snouts a few metres apart and opening their mouths within seconds of each other.
It is the first direct record of humpbacks cooperating on the seafloor. Which animal is the smartest team hunter?
first_comment: Each whale kept the same spot in the formation in 93 percent of hunts. Who else hunts this well as a team?
